files.reason: default_controller (2353-2364) canonicalizes current_exe(); for a rebuilt binary Linux reports '<path>/microcoder (deleted)' (the coder exe itself, or a path ending in ' (deleted)'), canonicalize fails, exe becomes None, and controller_candidates (2372) skips the beside-program engine and falls back to ~/.openagents/bin. Add fn controller_executable_path(exe: PathBuf) -> PathBuf that strips a trailing ' (deleted)' suffix, use it in default_controller without dropping the path on canonicalize failure, and keep the ~/.openagents/bin fallback only when nothing exists beside it. The new test goes in the existing mod tests (after 4468) next to the #10074 test.

answer.likely_change:
In crates/coder/src/task/autostart.rs, add `fn controller_executable_path(exe: PathBuf) -> PathBuf` that strips a trailing " (deleted)" from the path, and use it in default_controller (around line 2354) instead of relying on canonicalize() succeeding, so the uncanonicalized parent directory still supplies the freshly rebuilt microcoder beside the program. Keep controller_candidates' order (beside exe, then app bundle MacOS, then ~/.openagents/bin) so the installed copy is used only when nothing is beside the program.

Add a unit test in the same file's mod tests using a fake exe path ending in " (deleted)" under a tempdir that contains MICROCODER, asserting the returned candidate is the beside-program engine and not the ~/.openagents/bin copy.
acceptance: A current_exe path ending in ' (deleted)' is normalized by controller_executable_path to the path without that suffix.
When the running binary was rebuilt (path ends in ' (deleted)'), default_controller finds the microcoder beside the program rather than ~/.openagents/bin.
~/.openagents/bin/microcoder is used only when no engine exists beside the program or in the app bundle.
